faqs.question: What is Engineering?
faqs.answer: Engineering is the application of Science and mathematics for making properties of matter and the sources of energy in nature useful to people. It deals with the designing and application of machines across factories and industries and production of finished goods for human use. It is one of the most fundamental domains which is important for the development of any nation. All the essential services to humankind is dependent on engineering such as Medicine, Security, Telecommunications, Transportation, Housing and Food. Therefore, engineering is a promising field to establish one's career. know more about - Engineering courses

faqs.question: What is BTech full form? What is the duration of the course?
faqs.answer: Hello aspirant! Bachelor of Technology ( B Tech full form ) is an undergraduate engineering degree awarded to you after the course completion. The duration of B.Tech course is four years . You need to have PCM subjects in Class 12 with minimum 55-75% aggregate marks that may vary on the basis of the institution. Some fields offer an exception where you do not necessarily need Mathematics as a core subject, it is less common though. Candidates who pursue BTech in Lateral Entry can complete this course in three years. Lateral Entry BTech is offered to candidates after they have completed Diploma course in a relevant engineering field after which they can enter into B.Tech course straight into second year. So, if you are a diploma-holder, you can go for lateral entry option as well. Best wishes!

faqs.question: What is the B Tech course all about?
faqs.answer: BTech full form is Bachelor of Technology. BTech courses majorly cover the basic principles & applications of engineering disciplines. The BTech syllabus is designed in such a way so as to help you follow your preferred career path in various engineering fields. The vast domains of BTech courses offer a diverse range of specializations. You can also pursue MTech/M.E/MBA degrees after completing BTech courses. You can even go for short-term Diploma courses in Cyber Security and Ethical Hacking, Red Hat Certified Engineer, Robotics, Nanotechnology, Software Testing etc. From IT firms, and banks to automobile companies, production houses and research and development initiatives, skilled technical engineers are needed in every work domain and industry.

faqs.question: What are the basic Engineering courses requirements for admission?
faqs.answer: The basic BTech courses requirements differ on the basis of the course level, specialisation and the college offering the course. For BTech courses you are generally expected to have at least 50 to 60% marks in Class 12 board exams and for MTech at least 55 to 60% marks in your graduation and entrance exam scores. Top colleges like the IITs and NITs give BTech admission on the basis of valid entrance exam scores while several private colleges also consider students based on merit and/or GD and PI rounds. For Engineering Diploma courses, you should have passed Class 10 with at least 50% marks, with Science and Math subjects . Interestingly, you can also get lateral entry admission to the BTech course directly in the 2nd year after completing a 3-year engineering diploma. For a PhD in Engineering, you must have completed PG in a relevant field with at least 55% marks and cleared valid entrance tests .

faqs.question: What is the general BTech qualification?

faqs.question: Can you list some important B Tech subjects?
faqs.answer: Below are some of the general subjects that you can pick during your BTech studies, as these course will advance your technical and practical knowledge: Mathematics: A mathematical background includes understanding of Calculus, Linear Algebra, Differential Equations and Statistic Stamina. Physics: Mechanics, electricity & magnetism, kinetics & dynamics, thermodynamics and wave & optics. Chemistry: This common general chemistry course involves sub-topics such as organic chemistry, inorganic chemistry among others. Programming: C+,  Python,  Java Engineering fundamentals: Statistics, dynamics, fluids and their action, heat and its work, properties of matter Engineering design: Aesthetics, reasoning process, design tools and methods, using of computer-aided design (CAD). Rest, the subjects taught in the BTech courses would be specialization-specific, based on your chosen field.

faqs.question: Is B.Tech syllabus similar for all colleges?
faqs.answer: The BTech syllabus is not similar in all the Indian colleges. Talking about the first year of BTech, the general subjects taught are almost similar that include Physics, Mathematics, Chemistry and other engineering fundamentals to provide a basic foundation for the BTech course ahead. Further, the BTech syllabus will differ on the basis of the specialisation you have chosen and the college, different colleges follow their own set of guidelines regarding the course curriculum that includes both core and elective subjects along with practical lab work.

faqs.question: Are there any elective subjects in B.Tech course?
faqs.answer: BTech courses do offer a variety of electives for you to opt for in the 5th and 6th semesters, where you get the chance to pick a specific subject that interests you more and is easy-going for you. You can choose to pick a subject according to the specialised field within your broad BTech specialization, which you would like to enter into in the future, where you see yourself as a happy and well-established engineering professional. For example, in BTech Electrical Engineering, there are a variety of electives like Power Systems and Electronics, Signal Processing, Communication Systems Theory, VLSI Technology, etc. Know more about - BTech Syllabus

faqs.question: Is M.Tech syllabus same in all colleges?
faqs.answer: The MTech syllabus is not similar in all the Indian colleges. Talking about the first year of MTech, the general subjects taught are in line with the specialisation chosen by you in order to provide you with the foundational research knowledge of the subject area. Further, the M.Tech syllabus will differ on the basis of the specialisation you have chosen and the institution offering the M.Tech course, different colleges follow their own set of guidelines regarding the M.Tech course curriculum that includes both core and elective subjects along with project work in the last semester.
